text:
Do not sing, do not sing, for from far away come the shipwrecked,

come prisoners, one-eyed men, monks, orators,

suicides.

Doors come again, and the cold of stones,

of stairways,

and, in black clothing, those two ancient hands.

And a candle with a wavering smoky flame. And books. And

writings.

Do not sing, no. For it was the music of your

voice that was heard. I am recently dead, still

with tears.

Someone carelessly spat upon my eyelashes.

So I saw it was already late.


And I let the sun remain at my feet and the flies walk.

And a slow saliva slipped from my teeth.

Do not sing, for I have braided my hair, now,

and I stand before the mirror, and know well that I am fleeing.

translation.title: Do Not Sing
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. Portuguese original provenance is retained through the supplied Spanish version; its abrupt syntax and line breaks are preserved.
